newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat sees higher profits in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Fiat sees higher profits in 1997.

text.p: Fiat on Monday predicted considerably higher operating profits in 1997, driven by the success of an Italian car-buying incentive programme in Italy started this year.

Company Chairman Cesare Romiti told Fiat's annual shareholders meeting that margins in Fiat's car business had started to improve in March and that this, together with increased sales, would lead to better operating profits in 1997.
"Auto margins in the first quarter were much better in March because the incentive scheme took some time to take off, and April and May also showed this positive impact," he said.

In 1996, Fiat's operating income from its industrial activities was 2.1 trillion lire ($1.24 billion) on sales of around 78 trillion lire ($46 billion), but net profits were boosted by extraordinary items.

For this year, Romiti reiterated his message last month that 1997 sales would rise around 15 percent to 90 trillion lire ($53 billion) from the previous year while income before taxes should not fall short of 1996's 3.8 trillion-lire ($2.2 billion) level.
Italy's incentive programme, started in January and set to run to September, allows owners of cars older than 10 years to trade their vehicles in for scrapping in return for a discount on a new car.
